sentences.text: Pseudoruminococcus massiliensis was described as a new genus of the family Ruminococcaceae, isolated from the gut microbiota of a healthy Senegalese man.
A second strain, E10-96H, was isolated from a healthy faecal donor; the species is strictly anaerobic and had previously been represented only by its type strain.
That strain carries 20 glycoside hydrolase genes and degrades starch in vitro, which the authors suggest may contribute to fibre degradation, cross-feeding and butyrate production.
The strain also carries pilus-like structures, harbours pilin genes and adheres to enterocytes in vitro.
In stool metagenomes from 1762 participants undergoing colonoscopy, this species was among a small number of species modestly linked to colorectal neoplasia, particularly early lesions.
